items.what: Explicit ASC must be preserved verbatim as 'ASC' (not dropped) when generating duckdb SQL — the instruction only says sort order 'is not rendered', not that the fix is to keep explicit ASC tokens.
items.quote: "SELECT i FROM RANGE(5) AS _(i) ORDER BY i ASC"

items.what: Default (unspecified) and DESC orderings must round-trip unchanged, including for the default dialect — implied by the issue but not literally stated as required outputs.
strings: SELECT i FROM RANGE(5) AS _(i) ORDER BY i DESC
SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x
items.quote: "SELECT i FROM RANGE(5) AS _(i) ORDER BY i DESC"

items.what: In duckdb, 'ORDER BY x ASC NULLS LAST' must render as 'ORDER BY x ASC' — i.e. explicit NULLS LAST is dropped as the duckdb default. The instruction never mentions NULLS ordering, so dropping an explicitly-written modifier is extra semantics beyond 'preserve sort order'.
strings: SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x ASC
items.quote: parse_one("SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x ASC NULLS LAST").sql("duckdb"), "SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x ASC"

reason: The issue only demonstrates ASC being dropped; the tests additionally demand exact round-trip strings and that duckdb's default NULLS LAST is elided. The first two are the direct consequence of the requested fix; the NULLS LAST elision relies on duckdb's existing default null-order behavior in the generator, which makes it guessable but not stated.
